ambient_events: The ops radio coughs a burst of static and a clipped voice — a callsign, a heading — then goes back to hissing.
Somewhere behind the tarps two people are haggling in low, flat voices; the numbers stop the second you glance over.
A rope of avgas fumes drifts off the half-stripped flyer, sweet and headache-sharp in the cold hangar air.
Dust hangs in the work-lights in long slow spirals, stirred by nothing you can feel.
A wrench slips somewhere in the dark at the back and rings once off the concrete. Nobody goes to see whose.
The corrugated roof ticks and pops as the desert heat leans on it, then eases off.
Grit sifts in under the apron door with every gust and lays a fresh film over everything that was clean an hour ago.
A tarp corner lifts in the draught, shows a stencilled crate-mark that isn't any shipping line you know, and settles back down.
description: Corrugated walls sweating avgas and cold metal, a half-stripped flyer up on jacks, and cargo nobody's labelling stacked under tarps along the back wall. A flight-ops desk faces the apron door, its radio hissing quiet static. Whatever came in on the last plane is still here, and nobody's asking whose it is.

flags.intro_lore: Welcome to the Reach — a smear of light in a hundred miles of scrub, a long haul off every road the Architect ever paved. Most come in by air, and Buzzard Field is the easy door; the overland way is a gauntlet of dust and dead ground that eats anyone who tries it soft. They'll take your fuel money and your silence and, if you're the right kind of wrong, they'll let you stay. The Reach doesn't trust outsiders; it survives on the ones it lets in. Whatever you're running, nobody here will ask to see it.

name: The Hangar Bay
